editorial:
Imagine a washed-up scientist who thinks he's a genius, a smart assistant who actually does the work, and a loud survivalist all getting sucked into a weird world full of dinosaurs and slow-moving lizard people. That's the wild ride you're in for here. The movie leans hard into silly comedy and over-the-top adventure, mixing slapstick jokes with big action scenes. It doesn't take itself seriously for even a second, which is exactly the point. If you're looking for a goofy, loud, and colorful escape, this one delivers that energy from start to finish.

The cast clearly has fun with the material, and the creature effects are surprisingly solid for a comedy. The pacing moves quickly, though some jokes land better than others, and a few scenes run a little long. It's best enjoyed with friends who don't mind dumb humor and big laughs. endingExplained: In the final scenes, the trio discovers that the Sleestaks and their leader are trying to use the time vortex to take over Earth. After a chaotic battle, Rick uses his tachyon amplifier to reopen the portal. They escape back to their own time, but the portal also brings a dinosaur into the modern world. The movie ends with Rick becoming famous again, while Will and Holly adjust to normal life, leaving the door open for more adventures.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves goofy comedies and dinosaur adventures.
